items.summary: Manually-constructed protobuf-es v2 messages need $typeName as const and $unknown: undefined.
items.description: When constructing proto-compatible objects manually (not via create()), set $typeName as const and $unknown: undefined. Example: { ..., $typeName: 'dnd5e.api.v1alpha1.EntityPlacement' as const, $unknown: undefined }. This is a protobuf-es v2 requirement.

items.summary: Use optionsRef.current = options each render to avoid stale closures in long-lived stream callbacks.
items.description: In useEncounterStream, optionsRef.current = options on every render prevents stale closures inside long-lived async stream callbacks. Use this pattern in any hook that accepts callbacks and maintains async loops.

items.summary: Connect-buffer-snapshot-replay-sync is the canonical mid-stream encounter join sequence.
items.description: Connect stream, buffer events (isSyncingRef), fetch snapshot, replay buffer, set synced. This sequence in useEncounterStream is the canonical pattern for joining a real-time encounter mid-stream.

items.summary: useDungeonMap.mergeRoom accumulates state immutably via new Map/Set rather than mutation.
items.description: mergeRoom() in useDungeonMap is immutable — it never mutates input state. All geometry accumulation is via new Map/Set construction. Use this pattern for any state that needs to accumulate across events.

items.summary: wallKey() sorts endpoints lexicographically to dedupe shared walls across rooms.
items.description: wallKey(wall) canonicalizes wall endpoints by sorting them lexicographically, so the same physical wall shared between two rooms produces one map entry regardless of direction.

items.summary: Movement-style event consumers prefer updatedEntity but fall back on entityId + path[last] when the snapshot is missing.
items.description: Pattern for consumers of events that carry both an entity snapshot and a movement path: prefer the snapshot, but synthesize a position-only update from path[path.length-1] when the snapshot is absent. Drives applyEntityPositionUpdate in useEncounterState. The pure helper mergeEntityPosition is a no-op when the entity isn't already tracked — never fabricate entities from a position alone.

items.summary: Render every revealed room and every entity in unified state regardless of currentRoomId; never filter by entity.roomId === currentRoomId. Also INGEST every revealed room — don't read only data.rooms[currentRoomId].
items.description: currentRoomId is the player's location, not a render scope. Once a room is revealed, its tiles, walls, doors, and entities are first-class scene members until the encounter ends. Filtering renders or interactions by entity.roomId === currentRoomId hides the player when they enter a new room and breaks cross-room visibility. The accumulated dungeonMap.floorTiles + open-door walkable-keys define the walkable scene; A* and click handlers operate on the union, not on a per-room slice. Per feedback_no_logic_in_web — visibility decisions belong to the API. The ingest side is symmetric: when a RoomRevealed event lands, `data.currentRoomId` is still the player's previous room (opening a door doesn't move the player). The revealed room's RoomLayout lives in `data.rooms[<revealedId>]`. Helpers that materialize legacy Room objects from EncounterStateData must iterate `Object.keys(data.rooms)`, not just read `data.rooms[currentRoomId]` — otherwise the revealed room's floor tiles never get generated.
items.example: BattleMapPanel.tsx mapEntitiesForRender; HexGrid.tsx isBlocked + openDoorWalkableKeys; LobbyView.tsx roomsFromEncounterState

items.validated_in: PR #389 (slice 2 walking skeleton); extended in PR #395 (Wave 2.7) and PR #396 (Wave 2.8)
items.summary: v1alpha2 encounter consumes via useEncounterStream2 + typed dispatcher; reducers in useEncounterState
items.description:
Wave 2.5 slice 2 (PR #389) established the v2 consumer pattern; Waves 2.7 (PR #395) and 2.8 (PR #396) extended it without divergence. Three layers:

1. src/api/useEncounterStream2.ts — opens StreamEncounter via the v2 client, consumes the async iterator, dispatches typed events to a callback bag. Owns: AbortController unmount cleanup, exponential-backoff reconnect via shared RECONNECT_CONFIG, null encounterId (no-op until real id arrives). optionsRef.current = options is set every render to avoid stale closures inside the long-lived async loop.

2. src/api/encounterStream2Dispatch.ts — typed dispatcher. The v1alpha2 EncounterEvent is a oneof; the dispatcher narrows the union and calls the matching callback. As of Wave 2.8 the dispatcher handles 11 cases (snapshotDelivered, entityMoved, geometryRevealed, entityAppeared, entityDisappeared, doorOpened, entityDamaged, statusApplied, modeChanged, turnStarted, turnEnded). Unknown cases console.warn but do not tear the stream down. Add a new event type → add a callback + a dispatch case.

3. src/hooks/useEncounterState.ts — reducers that mutate the encounter's local model from event payloads. Wave 2.5 added applyHexRevealed/EntityAppeared/EntityDisappeared; Wave 2.7 added applyDoorOpened (idempotent); Wave 2.8 added applyEntityDamaged, applyStatusApplied, applyModeChanged, applyTurnStarted, applyTurnEnded (last is intentionally a no-op — TurnStarted is authoritative for the next actor). All reducers are pure, immutable, idempotent where meaningful.

Cause/effect split: cause-only events (DoorOpened, AttackResolved) are deliberately separated from effect events (GeometryRevealed, EntityDamaged, StatusApplied). The dispatcher does NOT collapse them; consumers subscribe to both.

When adding a new v2 event type: extend the dispatcher with the typed case AND add a reducer to useEncounterState (or note explicitly that this event is render-only with no state change).

items.summary: v1alpha2 unary RPCs each get their own hook in src/api/use<Verb>V2.ts; client lives at encounterClientV2

items.summary: PlaytestHarness (?encounterId= + ?playerId=, dev-only) is the wave-verification surface — temporary, slated for slice-3 deletion (#391)
items.description:
src/components/playtest/PlaytestHarness.tsx is the dev-only debug surface used to verify each v2 wave end-to-end. It renders connection state, entities table, revealed-hex set, recent-events log, and per-wave verification controls via the v2 hooks. Mounts via App.tsx when ?encounterId= is in the URL in dev mode.

Key conventions encoded by the harness:
  - Two-tab dev pattern: ?playerId=alice / ?playerId=bob URL params override the auth identity. useDevPlayerIdAuth(playerId) (useLayoutEffect) syncs the override into the gRPC auth store BEFORE any child useEffect, preventing a race where the first request goes out without the override applied.
  - Hardcoded seeded fallback positions (alice 0,0,0; bob 1,-1,0) — TEMPORARY workaround for the slice-1 empty SnapshotDelivered.encounter; removable once snapshot replay lands (rpg-api#497).
  - One section per wave: Move (slice 2), Open door (Wave 2.7, PR #395), Combat with Attack + End turn (Wave 2.8, PR #396). Each section is gated on relevant state (combat: mode==TURN_BASED && activeEntityId==localPlayerId).
  - Header carries every cross-cutting v2 indicator: connectionState, mode, activeEntityId, round, HP. New v2 fields land in the header as new waves add them.
  - Cause/effect log lines: every event type logs independently. On a single attack you see e.g. `EntityDamaged goblin-1 amount=5 hp_after=2/7` then `StatusApplied goblin-1 <- frightened` as two distinct lines. Don't collapse cause and effect in display.

The harness is slated for deletion in rpg-dnd5e-web#391 (slice 3) once LobbyView migrates to v2 for the verbs that have shipped. Don't build durable UI on top of the harness; per-wave sections are throwaway verification scaffolding.

items.validated_in: PR #389 (HexEntity ghost transition fix); validated against eight call sites across hex-grid components
items.summary: React Three Fiber runs frameloop="demand"; visual updates outside React state must call useThree().invalidate()
items.description:
The R3F canvas (HexGrid.tsx:544) is configured frameloop="demand" — frames render only when invalidated. State changes through React props/state invalidate automatically. But visual transitions driven outside React (uniform updates, ghost/visible toggles applied imperatively, ref-based shader writes, useFrame animations, instanced-mesh rebuilds, camera control inputs) must call invalidate() manually.

Wave 2.5 hit this in HexEntity.tsx ghost transitions (HexEntity.tsx:192-201): when isGhost flipped, the shader uniform updated but the next frame didn't render until something else invalidated. Fix: const { invalidate } = useThree(); useEffect(() => { invalidate(); }, [isGhost, invalidate]).

Validated call sites in src/components/hex-grid/: HexEntity (ghost flag), MediumHumanoid (useFrame ghostAmount uniform), InstancedHexTiles + ShadedHexFloor + ShadedHexWall (instance rebuilds), HexDoor (open animation), useCameraControls (pan/zoom/keyboard).

If you write code that mutates a uniform, swaps a material, toggles a mesh property, or rebuilds instanced geometry in a useEffect/useMemo without React knowing, also invalidate.

items.summary: DoorOpened toggles door open/closed; GeometryRevealed adds hexes — two reducers, one verb
items.description:
Wave 2.7 (rpg-dnd5e-web PR #395) shipped the consumer side of the cause/effect-event split for OpenDoor. The Interact verb on the API publishes TWO events: DoorOpenedEvent (cause: door state flips) and HexRevealedEvent / GeometryRevealed (effect: new room hexes are now visible). The web consumes them as TWO separate reducers in src/hooks/useEncounterState.ts:

  - applyDoorOpened(state, evt) — flips the door entry in state.doors (or appends if new). Idempotent: opening an already-open door is a no-op.
  - applyGeometryRevealed(state, evt) — appends hexes to state.revealedHexes (Set or array). Idempotent: re-revealing a hex is a no-op.

The dispatcher (encounterStream2Dispatch.ts) calls each reducer when its event type fires; do NOT collapse the two events into one combined reducer. Mirrors the API-side rule (pat-v2-cause-effect-event-split): cause and effect stay separate at every layer.

Why idempotent: snapshot-replay on reconnect can re-emit both events; reducers must tolerate that. See pat-v2-stream-hook-pattern for the broader reducer convention (pure, immutable, idempotent where meaningful).

When adding a new Interact target type (chest, lever, trap):
  - Each new toolkit verb produces its own cause + effect events. Add a reducer per event type, not per verb.
  - Test with a contrived double-fire (snapshot + live event of the same shape) to confirm idempotency.
items.example: src/hooks/useEncounterState.ts applyDoorOpened + applyGeometryRevealed; src/api/encounterStream2Dispatch.ts dispatch cases

items.summary: PlaytestHarness verb sections use a target-input + verb-button shape that's reusable for future Interact targets
Combat event reducers: EntityDamaged updates HP map; StatusApplied appends to status list; ModeChanged updates mode; TurnStarted updates activeEntityId + round
items.description:
Wave 2.8 (rpg-dnd5e-web PR #396) added five reducers to src/hooks/useEncounterState.ts for the combat events:

  - applyEntityDamaged(state, evt) — updates state.entities[targetId].hp = { current: evt.hp_after.current, max: evt.hp_after.max }. The event carries hp_after authoritatively; do NOT subtract evt.amount from local hp (server is source of truth, races possible).
  - applyStatusApplied(state, evt) — appends evt.condition_ref to state.entities[targetId].statuses. Tolerates the entity not yet existing (no-op + console.warn).
  - applyModeChanged(state, evt) — replaces state.mode with evt.new_mode. Triggers UI re-gating (combat section enables/disables).
  - applyTurnStarted(state, evt) — updates state.activeEntityId = evt.active_entity_id and state.round = evt.round. Authoritative for whose turn it is.
  - applyTurnEnded(state, evt) — intentionally a no-op. TurnStarted is authoritative; TurnEnded fires for animation hooks / log lines but doesn't change activeEntityId. Don't clear it on TurnEnded — between TurnEnded(actorA) and TurnStarted(actorB) the harness would briefly show no active actor.

All five reducers are pure, immutable, idempotent where meaningful. Same convention as pat-v2-stream-hook-pattern.

NPC turn cycle: one EndTurn RPC produces multiple events (validated 2026-05-09 — bob ends → 5 events: TurnEnded(bob), TurnStarted(goblin), EntityDamaged(alice), TurnEnded(goblin), TurnStarted(alice round=2)). Each reducer fires independently as its event arrives; don't try to collapse the cycle into one batch.

When adding more combat events (HealReceived, ConditionRemoved, Knockback, etc.): one reducer per event type, no shared mutation.
items.example: src/hooks/useEncounterState.ts applyEntityDamaged + applyStatusApplied + applyModeChanged + applyTurnStarted + applyTurnEnded

items.summary: PlaytestHarness header carries the mode indicator + dev-only mode-flip control; combat sections gate on mode === TURN_BASED
items.description:
Wave 2.8 added a mode indicator to the PlaytestHarness header: the current encounter.mode (FREE_ROAM | TURN_BASED) is displayed prominently alongside connectionState, activeEntityId, round, HP. The harness also exposes a dev-only mode-flip control (slated to come from CreateEncounter(initial_mode=TURN_BASED) + a future SetMode RPC; for Wave 2.8 the playtest seed sets mode at creation time).

Gating: combat sections (Attack, End Turn) are only rendered when:

  state.mode === 'TURN_BASED' && state.activeEntityId === localPlayerId

When mode flips back to FREE_ROAM (future waves), combat sections disappear cleanly because of this gate. The Move section is mode-agnostic and stays available in any mode.

The header is the cross-cutting v2 indicator surface — every new wave that adds a top-level Encounter field (Wave 2.6 added activeEntityId/round, Wave 2.8 added mode + HP) lands its display in the header. New v2 fields land in the header before they land in any per-section UI.

Don't promote the harness mode-flip control to durable UI. Mode-flip in the real game flows from narrative triggers (ambush, door-opens-into-combat) on the API side; the harness is a verification surface, not a user-facing control.

Future: when SetMode RPC ships (probably Wave 2.10+), the harness gets a real flip button. Until then, encounter mode is set at CreateEncounter time only.
items.example: src/components/playtest/PlaytestHarness.tsx header (mode + activeEntityId + round + HP); combat section gating expression

items.summary: LocalEncounterState must carry every field the snapshot projects; when API ships new fields, the web reducer must consume them
items.description:
Discovered during Wave 2.8 playtest 2026-05-09. The combat live-event reducers in PR #396 worked correctly — incoming EntityDamaged + StatusApplied + ModeChanged + TurnStarted updated LocalEncounterState as expected. But the SnapshotDelivered handler (initial connect / reconnect) lagged behind the API's projection in three places:

  - rpg-dnd5e-web#397: onEntityAppeared in PlaytestHarness built a v1alpha1 EntityState stub with EntityType.UNSPECIFIED instead of consuming the v1alpha2 Entity from the event — discarded type, hp, and the data oneof (MonsterData / CharacterData).
  - rpg-dnd5e-web#398: harness entities table had no HP column even though the snapshot now carried HP per entity.
  - rpg-dnd5e-web#399: harness had no initiative-order display even though the snapshot's TurnState now carried initiative_order.
  - rpg-dnd5e-web#400: combat-enabled gate read myEntityId only — needed to also check activeEntityId === localPlayerId once turn state was actually projected.

The pattern these all share: when the API ships a new field on the snapshot Encounter / Entity / TurnState shape, LocalEncounterState (and the SnapshotDelivered → state reducer) MUST consume that field, even if a corresponding live event also updates it. Otherwise:
  - Fresh client connects → snapshot has the field → state ignores it → UI gates broken until a live event arrives.
  - Refresh mid-encounter → same problem.

Wave checklist whenever the rpg-api side adds a field to the projected Encounter / Entity / TurnState:
  1. Extend LocalEncounterState type to carry it.
  2. Update the SnapshotDelivered → state initialization to read it.
  3. (If a live event also updates it) update that reducer too — same field, two paths.
  4. Update the harness header / table to display it (per pat-v2-mode-flip-ui).
  5. Manual seed-and-refresh test: confirm the field shows up on a cold connect, not just after a live event.

Mirrors the API-side pat-v2-projection-and-events-must-stay-in-sync rule. Live events and snapshot projection are TWO paths on every layer.
items.example: src/hooks/useEncounterState.ts LocalEncounterState type + applySnapshotDelivered; src/components/playtest/PlaytestHarness.tsx entities table (HP column) + initiative display + combat gate

items.summary: pendingPrompt: InputRequired | null lives in encounter state; modal renders when set; cleared on SubmitCheck resolution
items.description:
Wave 2.9 (rpg-dnd5e-web PR #403) added `pendingPrompt: InputRequired | null` to LocalEncounterState in src/hooks/useEncounterState.ts and a `setPendingPrompt(prompt)` reducer to mutate it. The PlaytestHarness renders a SkillCheckPromptModal whenever `state.pendingPrompt !== null && state.pendingPrompt.kind.case === 'skill_check'`:

  - Modal carries a header ("Skill check: {ability} (DC {dc}), tool: {tool}"), a number input for the d20 roll (1-20), and a Submit button wired to useSubmitCheckV2.
  - Other prompt kinds (`dialogue`, `target_select`) render a placeholder ("not yet supported") for Wave 2.9. Future waves wire them.
  - On SubmitCheck success the caller calls `setPendingPrompt(null)` (see v2-rpc-response-side-effect for who calls what when).

The state is encounter-scoped (one slot per encounter) — single-pending is enforced server-side per pat-v2-pending-prompt-collision; the web mirrors with a single nullable field, no queue.

When adding a new prompt kind to the modal: add a switch case on `pendingPrompt.kind.case` in the modal render block, NOT a parallel state field. Keep one state slot, multiple render branches.

PlaytestHarness is the verification surface for Wave 2.9 (per pat-v2-playtest-harness). LobbyView migration to a real prompt UI is Wave 5+ work; build the durable design against the validated harness shape rather than co-evolving.

items.summary: Auto-clear timer for prompt-modal results uses a prompt-identity check before clearing; prevents a stale 2s timer from clobbering a newer incoming prompt

EntityRemoved is the entities-table reducer that drops the entry; reducer is idempotent for snapshot-after-removal. EntityDied is optional-render (transient log/animation), not a state-mutation reducer
items.description:
Wave 2.10 (rpg-dnd5e-web PR #405) shipped the consumer side of the cause/effect-event split for entity death (mirrors api-side pat-v2-cause-effect-death-events). The toolkit publishes TWO events on a kill: `EntityDiedEvent` (cause: dying actor, killer attribution, narrative payload) and `EntityRemovedEvent` (effect: actor gone from world). Web treats them ASYMMETRICALLY:

  - applyEntityRemoved(state, evt) — STATE MUTATION reducer in src/hooks/useEncounterState.ts. Drops `state.entities[evt.entityId]` from the map. IDEMPOTENT: no-op if the entity is already missing. This idempotency is load-bearing — late-joiners get a snapshot WITHOUT the dead entity, then the live event stream may also fire EntityRemoved for the same id (snapshot-replay race). Reducer must tolerate.
  - EntityDiedEvent — OPTIONAL-RENDER. Hooks into log lines ("alice slays the goblin") and death animations. NOT wired as a state-mutation reducer because nothing on LocalEncounterState changes from the cause alone. Future waves that add a death-throes animation queue or a kill-attribution overlay will subscribe to EntityDied; today it's logged in the harness events panel and that's it.

The dispatcher (encounterStream2Dispatch.ts) calls each reducer/handler when its event fires; do NOT collapse the two into one combined reducer. Mirrors api-side pat-v2-cause-effect-death-events: cause and effect stay separate at every layer.

Why idempotent: snapshot-replay on reconnect emits a snapshot with the dead entity already gone, then the live stream may re-emit EntityRemoved if it was buffered during the replay. Reducer treats either ordering as safe.

When adding a new entity-lifecycle event (Resurrected, Banished, Polymorphed): one reducer per event type. Cause events log/animate; effect events mutate state. Same as Wave 2.7's DoorOpened (cause) + GeometryRevealed (effect) split.
items.example: src/hooks/useEncounterState.ts applyEntityRemoved (idempotent delete); src/api/encounterStream2Dispatch.ts entityDied + entityRemoved cases; src/components/playtest/PlaytestHarness.tsx events log shows EntityDied as a transient line

items.summary: useEncounterState exposes encounterStatus: 'active' | 'ended' (string union, not boolean) — set by EncounterEnded event handler; snapshot replay sets it on connect for already-ended encounters
items.description:
Wave 2.10 (rpg-dnd5e-web PR #405) added `encounterStatus: 'active' | 'ended'` to LocalEncounterState in src/hooks/useEncounterState.ts. Set by:

  - applyEncounterEnded(state, evt) — flips state.encounterStatus from 'active' to 'ended'. IDEMPOTENT: re-firing on an already-ended encounter is a no-op. Also clears any per-actor turn UI gates that should disappear at end (active-action button enable expressions naturally evaluate to false because activeEntityId logic short-circuits on encounterStatus === 'ended').
  - SnapshotDelivered handler — when joining mid-encounter or reconnecting to a terminal encounter, the snapshot reducer reads the snapshot's terminal-state markers (entity table empty of monsters, no active actor in TurnState, etc.) AND the API includes encounter-end marker in projection (per pat-v2-snapshot-reducer-must-read-all-fields, snapshot must consume every projected field). Sets encounterStatus = 'ended' on connect.

String union, NOT boolean: deliberately leaves room for future states ('escaped' for player-fled, 'paused' for narrative pause, 'failed' for TPK). A boolean `isEnded` would force a parallel field per state; a single union scales additively.

UI conditionally renders end-state indicators based on this field: PlaytestHarness shows an "Encounter ended" banner when encounterStatus === 'ended', disables verb buttons, and stops accepting input. Per feedback_no_logic_in_web: web doesn't enforce — server returns FailedPrecondition on any verb against an ended encounter (api pat-v2-terminal-encounter-state). The web disables to match the server's enforcement so users don't get a confusing error toast on a button they could see was inert.

When adding a new terminal status ('escaped', 'paused'): extend the union, add a reducer for the corresponding API event. Keep one state field, multiple values.

Mirrors api-side pat-v2-mode-ended-wire-mapping: the web doesn't read the wire mode field for end detection (mode stays FREE_ROAM after end on the wire by current proto contract); it reads the dedicated EncounterEnded event.
items.example: src/hooks/useEncounterState.ts encounterStatus + applyEncounterEnded reducer + SnapshotDelivered terminal-detection branch; src/components/playtest/PlaytestHarness.tsx end-banner + verb-button disable expressions

items.summary: Three known display drifts after EntityRemoved/EncounterEnded that the harness doesn't currently update via reducer; server enforcement is correct, these are display-only — fix in future waves that touch the harness
items.description:
Discovered during Wave 2.10 playtest 2026-05-09 and filed as rpg-dnd5e-web#406. After an `EntityRemoved` (monster dies) or `EncounterEnded` event, three pieces of display state drift out of sync because the corresponding reducer doesn't update them:

  1. `state.initiativeOrder` does NOT drop dead actors. Initiative array still contains the removed entity id; the harness's initiative display shows the dead goblin in the order until reconnect (snapshot-replay rebuilds it from authoritative data).
  2. `state.activeEntityId` stays set after EncounterEnded. If the encounter ends on a TurnEnded event without a subsequent TurnStarted (which is correct toolkit behavior — no next turn), the activeEntityId points to the last actor who acted. Combat sections gate on `activeEntityId === localPlayerId` so they may briefly enable/disable incorrectly until snapshot replay.
  3. `state.mode` header does NOT reflect end. Per api pat-v2-mode-ended-wire-mapping, the wire mode field stays FREE_ROAM (no _ENDED enum value yet). The harness reads state.mode to display "FREE_ROAM" / "TURN_BASED"; with no ENDED option, it shows whatever mode was last set. The dedicated `encounterStatus: 'ended'` carries the correct end signal but the header doesn't override the mode display from it.

**Server enforcement is correct** — verbs return FailedPrecondition for any state-mutating call against an ended encounter (api pat-v2-terminal-encounter-state). Combat-section disable also gates on encounterStatus, so users can't actually invoke a stale-displayed verb. These are display-only drifts.

Fix path (future wave that touches the harness; tracked as rpg-dnd5e-web#406):
  - Extend applyEntityRemoved to splice initiativeOrder (filter out the removed id; if currentTurn pointed past the new length, wrap or clear).
  - Extend applyEncounterEnded (or add applyTurnEnded check) to clear activeEntityId when encounterStatus flips to 'ended'.
  - Add display override in the harness header: when encounterStatus === 'ended', show "ENDED" instead of state.mode.

Don't fix this in Wave 2.10 — it shipped + verified end-to-end; user impact is zero. Promote to a wave that's already touching PlaytestHarness or LobbyView. Keep this pattern as the playbook so a future agent doesn't reinvent the diagnosis.

Lesson: not every display drift is a bug worth fixing immediately. When server enforcement is correct, display-only drifts can be deferred behind durable issue tracking. Per feedback_checkpoint_over_rabbit_hole.

items.summary: Custom THREE.ShaderMaterial used on InstancedMesh must explicitly multiply by instanceMatrix; Three.js does not auto-rewrite custom vertexShader source.
items.description: Three.js's WebGLProgram auto-defines USE_INSTANCING and adds the `attribute mat4 instanceMatrix;` declaration when a material is bound to an InstancedMesh, but it does NOT rewrite a ShaderMaterial's user-supplied vertexShader source. The shader author is responsible for `vec4 mvPosition = modelViewMatrix * instanceMatrix * vec4(position, 1.0);` (and `mat3(instanceMatrix) * normal` for lighting) inside `#ifdef USE_INSTANCING`. Likewise, USE_INSTANCING_COLOR + `attribute vec3 instanceColor;` for per-instance color — pass through a varying. Without the multiply, every instance renders at the geometry's local origin, which collapses an entire InstancedMesh into one stack at world (0,0,0). Symptoms can be mistaken for 'tile generation broken' when in reality the data layer is correct and the GPU is just rendering all instances on top of each other.
items.example: src/shaders/AdvancedCharacterShader.ts vertex shader USE_INSTANCING block; src/components/hex-grid/ShadedHexFloor.tsx uses InstancedMesh + this material
